topology.rule: The prints disagree. Where the lower bowl's terminal meets the diagonal, the leaflet (N46, and the flyer scan) joins them and closes the counter; the brochure (N45, and Trinity's copy B2: the same plate) leaves a sliver of paper about one source pixel (10 font units) wide. A gap one print shows and another fills is taken as print: the join is kept closed, as N46 draws it and Study 3 has it. Against this: both brochure copies show the gap, and the photocopy prints about 10% heavier, enough to close a drawn sliver. Open question.

limitations: N46/N45 can share artwork or reproduction history; source fit is not independent authentication.
Legacy builder text-height regularisation and modern extensions remain.
Tuam accented entries supply accent geometry; final accents are assembled for text.

Without a production sheet the weight and contrast of the design are not settled: N46 (photocopy) prints its stems heavier and its hairlines thinner than N45 (offset); Study 4 takes the median print's stems (about 3% lighter than Study 3) and the prints' mean contrast.

sit_on_baseline.eight: N46 sets the 8 about 2 px (0.7 trace units) higher on its line than 0, 1, 2, 6 and the pound (feet at 1853 against a median of 1855 px); N45 sets it level with them (858 against 858). Placement on a paste-up is setting, not drawing: the 8 sits on the baseline like the other figures.

bold_keep_apart.why: Every print sets the dot of ! and ? clear of its stroke (Study 4 Regular: 13 and 17 units). The bold's wider pen leaves the ? dot 1.6 units from the stroke without joining it (Study 3: 5), so the bold keeps nothing to reopen and the sloped bold's hair of weight joins them. Set apart as the bold sets apart a dot it joins: a cut F_PASS of the regular's gap wide along the midline (bolden._separate, close).

derived_styles.sound_sloped_growth: The sloped styles' hair of weight (build2 condense) on oe comes out of pathops unsound (part of the e resolved as a hole, the eye lost); the outline simplified first grows soundly. Only oe in the Italic is affected; every other growth is unchanged.

N46.what: D. O'Sullivan leaflet, NIVAL copy (photocopy); Study 3's source for 50 letters

flyer.what: the release's scan of the same leaflet, about a third of N46's resolution

N45.what: competition brochure, NIVAL copy (offset); a separate paste-up; Study 3 b, e, e.alt1, h

B2.what: Bolger vol. 2 fig. 203b: Trinity College's copy of the brochure, photographed; half N45's resolution

N44.what: brochure cover heading "design an irish typeface", set in Céilí (Bolger vol. 1, pp. 279-80)

S53915.what: 24 pt Letraset sheet S53915 sample "a1" on the leaflet (N46)

S53916.what: 42 pt Letraset sheet S53916 sample "a1" on the leaflet (N46)

consensus.method: Each print registered onto the Study 3 trace by a similarity (uniform scale, rotation, shift: translation search, coarse-to-fine least squares), then twice onto the averaged prints' mean, the frame pinned in the trace's coordinates; mean of the high-resolution prints, each at its own midpoint, on a 0.125 trace-unit grid; edge at the face's one level (edge_level: the means' stems as wide as the median print's); fitted with curvefit3.contour_to_curves4; the frame is Study 3's.

disagreements.rule:
Where N46 and N45 (`prints`: their names and maps, each at its own midpoint) disagree by more than
edge noise, which print is drawing. A region one print inks and the other leaves white is
  - a notch, gap or dropout in the other print when the other's outline, closed by a disc of NOTCH, covers it: it is drawn (a gap or notch one print shows and another fills is print);
  - otherwise a protrusion of the inking print beyond the other. The cover heading N44, which is not averaged, votes where it prints the letter. Without a vote, a protrusion of N45 (a tip or spur the photocopy lost: it loses fine ends, the offset print does not) is drawn, and a lump of N46's toner thicker than 2 * BLOB is not; N46's thinner excess along its edges is its heavier weight, which the face's edge level already accounts for, and is left to the mean.

holdout_N44.note:
A check the averaging did not see: the cover heading N44 against N46 and N45 combined without it.
Shape agreement only (IoU, each N44 impression thresholded to the candidate's own ink area, so that
the prints' weights are set aside). N44 shares the brochure's press with N45, so N45 alone is not a
fair comparison; Study 3 and N46 are.

kept.DOTS: the legacy cluster; discarded by the builder

consensus.caveat: The prints reproduce one artwork. Averaging lowers each reproduction's noise (photocopy toner on N46, offset ink and paper on N45); it does not confirm the design. The weight is a calibration, not a measurement: at their own midpoints N45's stems print about 10% lighter than N46's and N44's, its hairlines no lighter.
